source_title: Diverse GABAergic neurons organize into subtype-specific sublaminae in the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
section: | Do laminated retinorecipient circuits organize visual pathways through the vLGN?
node_relevance_reason: Directly characterises GABAergic cell types (Ecel1, Pvalb, Spp1, Penk) in retinorecipient vLGNe.
summary: Anterograde trans-synaptic tracing shows Ecel1+, Pvalb+, Spp1+ and Penk+ GABAergic cells in vLGNe sublaminae are retinorecipient; none were found in vLGNi. Some subtypes are likely projection neurons. vLGNe is composed of at least four adjacent, transcriptionally distinct sublaminae of GABAergic neurons, many receiving direct retinal input; this laminar organization is absent from IGL.
quotes: Using anterograde trans-synaptic tracing, we identified Ecel1 + , Pvalb + , Spp1 + , and Penk + cells as retinorecipient, together representing at least three sublaminae of vLGNe.
While we failed to observe any retinorecipient cells in vLGNi using this method
we revealed a remarkably organized laminar architecture of vLGNe, composed of at least four adjacent, transcriptionally distinct sublaminae.

source_title: Retinal Input Is Required for the Maintenance of Neuronal Laminae in the Ventrolateral Geniculate Nucleus
section: Subtype-specific laminae are specified in the neonatal vLGN
node_relevance_reason: Describes vLGNe subtype-specific GABAergic layers (Ecel1/Lypd1, Penk) and their development.
summary: vLGNe can be divided into at least four subtype-specific layers of molecularly distinct neurons, several receiving monosynaptic retinal input; Lypd1+ and Ecel1+ cells are the same GABAergic subtype. vLGNe is identified as the area occupied by retinal axons and expands from 60% to 72% of vLGN postnatally.
quotes: vLGNe can be further divided into at least four subtype-specific layers, each composed of molecularly and functionally distinct neurons, several of which receive direct monosynaptic input from the retina (Sabbagh et al., 2021).
indicating that these markers correspond to the same GABAergic neuronal subtype.
The rodent vLGN can be divided into two distinct domains based on cytoarchitecture: the retinorecipient external division (vLGNe) and the nonretinorecipient internal division (vLGNi).

source_title: A High‐Resolution Transcriptomic Atlas of Cell Types in the Ventral Visual Thalamus
section: | Most Neuronal Types in vLGN Are Retinorecipient
node_relevance_reason: snRNA-seq of retinorecipient vLGN neurons mapping to inhibitory (Gad1/Gad2) clusters.
summary: AAV1-Cre transsynaptic tracing plus snRNA-seq of retinorecipient vLGN nuclei; retinorecipient cells fall in most clusters including inhibitory ones, though some excitatory clusters too.
quotes: Of note, these retinorecipient cells were evenly distributed among clusters and included clusters positive for excitatory markers (clusters 12 and 13).

source_title: Pattern of Driver-Like Input onto Neurons of the Mouse Ventral Lateral Geniculate Nucleus
node_relevance_reason: Differential marker expression (Pvalb, Penk, Nxph1 in vLGNe; Calb, Arx in vLGNi) and GABAergic majority.
summary: Most vLGN neurons are GABAergic; parvalbumin and proenkephalin neurons reside exclusively in vLGNe, Nxph1 mRNA is confined to vLGNe, and vLGNe receives driver-like retinal input.
quotes: traditional markers of neurochemically defined GABAergic neurons, such as parvalbumin-, calbindin-, and proenkephalin-expressing neurons, are differentially expressed in these regions with parvalbumin-and proenkephalin-expressing neurons residing exclusively in vLGNe and calbindin-expressing neurons residing in vLGNi
with Neurexophilin-1 (Nxph1) mRNA being confined to vLGNe

source_title: Not a one-trick pony: Diverse connectivity and functions of the rodent lateral geniculate complex
summary: vLGNe is the magnocellular, large-celled, densely retinorecipient external lamina; vLGN has few glutamatergic neurons and no stereotypic thalamocortical relay cells, being GABAergic-dominated.
quotes: the magnocellular external vLGN (vLGNe), which contains large cells and receives dense innervation from retina
vLGN contains a vastly higher population of GABAergic neurons

source_title: Divergent outputs of the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus mediate visually evoked defensive behaviors
section: Divergent vLGN outputs exert opposite influences on defensive behaviors
node_relevance_reason: vLGN GABA (Gad2+) neurons project to superior colliculus and nucleus reuniens; not vLGNe-specific.
summary: Gad2-Cre labelling shows vLGN GABA axons in SC and Re, via distinct output pathways; manipulating them affects defensive behaviour.
quotes: We observed GFP-expressing vLGN GABA axons in the SC (Figure 5B) and in the Re (Figures 5C and S3)

source_title: A visual circuit related to the parabrachial nucleus for the antipruritic effects of bright light treatment.
node_relevance_reason: RGCs innervate GABAergic vLGN/IGL neurons projecting to lateral parabrachial nucleus (matches node axon target).
summary: A subset of RGCs innervates GABAergic vLGN/IGL neurons that inhibit CaMKIIa+ LPBN neurons; vLGN/IGL-to-LPBN projection reduces itch. Region is vLGN/IGL, not vLGNe specifically.
quotes: a subset of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) innervates GABAergic neurons in the ventral lateral geniculate nucleus and intergeniculate leaflet (vLGN/IGL), which subsequently inhibit CaMKIIα+ neurons in the LPBN.

source_title: A Role for Thalamic Projection GABAergic Neurons in Circadian Responses to Light
node_relevance_reason: Sox14+ GABAergic IGL/LGv neurons projecting to lateral habenula.
summary: IGL/LGv neurons inhibit lateral habenula neurons; thalamic GABAergic projection neurons are defined by Sox14; IGL/LGv lacks obvious M1 ipRGC input.
quotes: Neurons in the IGL/LGv were shown to participate in mood regulation via inhibitory synapses onto lateral habenula (LH) neurons (Huang et al., 2019)
Hence, the mature IGL and LGv are characterized by a heterogenous cellular composition that includes Sox14 1 GABAergic thalamic neurons.

source_title: Nuclei-specific differences in nerve terminal distribution, morphology, and development in mouse visual thalamus
node_relevance_reason: vLGNe naming and non-image-forming inputs/outputs; GABA terminals.
summary: Defines vLGN (external division) function and inputs: non-image-forming RGCs and layer V cortex project to vLGN.
quotes: Layer VI cortical neurons project to dLGN, whereas layer V cortical neurons project to vLGN [24,35,36].

source_title: Nuclei-specific differences in nerve terminal distribution, morphology, and development in mouse visual thalamus
node_relevance_reason: Inhibitory terminals most abundant in vLGN; retinal terminals more abundant in vLGN.
summary: Inhibitory (GAD67/GAD65/VGAT) terminals are most abundant in vLGN, and retinal synapses there are not driver-like. Retinal terminals in vLGN differ from dLGN; background for vLGN inputs.
quotes: Inhibitory terminals (which contained GAD67, GAD65, or VGAT) are most abundant in vLGN.

Retino-recipient nuclei in a wide variety of mammalian brains are subdivided into discrete laminae (or regions), a feature that facilitates the flow of visual information through distinct parallel pathways in the brain.

source_title: Enhancement and contextual modulation of visuospatial processing by thalamocollicular projections from ventral lateral geniculate nucleus
node_relevance_reason: vLGN VGAT+ neurons project to superficial SC; vLGN heterogeneous with molecularly distinct sublaminae.
summary: vLGN VGAT+ axons project strongly to superficial SC; authors note vLGN comprises multiple molecularly distinct sublaminae.
quotes: Anatomically, our anterograde tracing reveals projections of vLGN VGAT+ axons more strongly to the superficial layers of SC (Fig. 1k)

source_title: An autoradiographic study of the projections from the lateral geniculate body of the rat.
node_relevance_reason: Classical autoradiographic vLGN projections in rat; no GABA/lamina specificity.
summary: vLGN in rat projects widely to pretectal nuclei, SC, zona incerta and others; no division into vLGNe/vLGNi.
quotes: In conclusion, the vast range of projections from the vLGN shows that this nucleus is important in many subcortical visual functions.

source_title: Retinal inputs signal astrocytes to recruit interneurons into visual thalamus
node_relevance_reason: States vLGN/IGL have a high fraction of GABAergic cells that are heterogeneous.
summary: Higher fraction of vLGN and IGL cells are GABAergic than dLGN, with heterogenous types; focus on interneuron recruitment.
quotes: In contrast to the dLGN (and neocortex), a significantly higher fraction of cells in the vLGN and IGL are GABAergic

source_title: Sonic hedgehog-dependent recruitment of GABAergic interneurons into the developing visual thalamus
node_relevance_reason: Region-level statement on vLGN/IGL non-image-forming roles.
summary: vLGN and IGL contribute to non-image-forming functions; principal neurons differ between dLGN and vLGN/IGL.
quotes: the vLGN and IGL contributing more to non-image-forming visual functions
